slices.name: ws01-27-chess-data-tables
slices.brief:
WS01 slice 27 of 32 (checkpoint D, the design system; slices 20 to 32; its draft PR is #108). Branch redesign/ws01-design-system, HEAD a12c74e (slice 26); the base for diffs is a12c74e. Checkpoints A, B and C are merged to main and live. Read first: REDESIGN_STATUS.md (Ordering rules, lines 7 to 11; the acceptance table with its AC6 row (line 30, still Planned: this slice fills it), its AC5 row (line 29), AC14 row (line 38) and T2 row (line 58) as the pattern for a filled row, its AC8 row (line 32, which counts the fixture page's badges and Buttons) and its AC13 row (line 37, step 31's); the step 26 block (lines 688 to 728) and the step 25 block (lines 653 to 686); Decisions (Mono figures and the focus ring from step 21, line 919; ScrollPanel from step 26, line 921, which hands the bounded table area to this slice; White and Black markers from step 27, line 922, which this slice makes true or rewords; the one monospace face from step 22, line 790); Deviations (the monospace face needs no feature settings, step 21, line 1008; Step 26, lines 1054 to 1064); Verify items (Mono font from step 21, line 1169; src/lib/format.ts from step 3, line 1078; the step 26 ones, lines 1225 to 1239); Follow-ups (Muted StatusBadge contrast from step 20, line 1330; Classes only docs and tests name reach the CSS from step 23, line 1348; The a11y servers share one database from step 23, line 1354; What printing leaves from step 24, line 1366; K reviews the step 26 judgement calls, line 1378; ScrollPanel on the long screens, line 1379); and the Printing bullet of the step 24 block, line 634), docs/redesign/REDESIGN_SPEC.md (Chess data, lines 299 to 301; table primitives, line 306; the files, lines 329 and 339; acceptance criterion 6, line 353; the planned format tests, line 364; what Crosstable prints today, line 1129; WS07's merge of the two tables into one component, line 1212; the WS01 deviations list, line 112, which carries step 26's sentence), docs/redesign/DESIGN_REPLAN_phase0.md (line 105: tiebreaks print as 13½, never 13.5; lines 117 and 590: one monospace face for chess data in every look, so one ResultCell and one standings design), the board the shapes come from (the manifest entry names none): docs/redesign/lca-redesign-boards/boards/Live-C.dc.html (figures right-aligned in the monospace face at 13px with the points at 15px, lines 31 to 34; the result cell .rc, 24px high with a 6px radius, a 58px minimum width, a 4px gap and 13px words in weight 500, its win, loss, draw and not-played tints, and the 8px white (a 1.5px ring) and black (filled) markers in the words' colour, lines 36 to 47; the rows from line 223, for example W, the marker, then 17), src/components/ui/table.tsx (all 117 lines), src/areas/live/components/Crosstable.tsx (all 100), StandingsTable.tsx (all 71) and ResultsEntry.tsx (lines 13 to 17 and 128 to 192), src/pages/TournamentPairingsPage.tsx (lines 28 to 36, 101 to 121 and 262 to 294), src/pages/TournamentPrintPage.tsx (lines 25 to 33, 86 to 117 and 157 to 197), src/pages/TournamentManagePage.tsx (lines 149, 2154, 2207 to 2229 and 2281 to 2318), src/pages/TournamentDetailPage.tsx (lines 634 to 668 and 755, the page the baseline samples), domain/format/score.ts with domain/format/index.ts and src/lib/format.ts, src/lib/features.ts, src/index.css (the monospace token at lines 44 to 46, 250 and 416; the surface tokens at 227 to 233, 398 to 404, 459 to 465, 504 to 510, 553 to 559 and 604 to 610; the status tokens at 252 to 261, 417 to 426, 473 to 482 and 526 to 541; ok and bad at 235, 236, 406, 407, 467, 468, 512 and 513), src/pages/fixtures/ScopeFixturePage.tsx (all 281 lines), src/components/ScrollPanel.tsx and src/lib/brand.ts (ADMIN_SCROLL, line 50), the tests that pin tables and scores today: test/unit/format.test.ts (lines 15 to 55 and 220 to 223), test/unit/format-edges.test.ts (lines 107 to 134), test/integration/domain-format.test.ts (lines 16 to 19), the glyph test test/unit/*mono-glyphs.test.ts (lines 96 to 123), test/unit/news-pinned-flag.test.tsx (lines 15 to 29, a switch flipped inside one file) with news-pinned.test.tsx and news-pinned-off.test.tsx, test/unit/status-dot-newlook.test.tsx (the mock of src/lib/features), test/unit/contrast.test.ts (lines 698 to 728), test/unit/base-components-scope.test.ts (lines 80 to 98), test/unit/goldText.test.ts (lines 799 to 804), test/unit/browser-test-wiring.test.ts (lines 340 to 400 and the dash check at 456 to 490), test/unit/redesign-status-step26.test.ts with the earlier record tests (steps 23 to 25 and the checkpoint C one), and the browser harness (playwright.config.ts, test/a11y/support.ts, baseline.ts, baseline.json, builds.spec.ts lines 96 to 105 and 139 to 151, tokens.spec.ts lines 132 to 146 and 208 to 217, print-look.spec.ts, seeded-data.spec.ts lines 205 to 228, components.spec.ts as the pattern for a spec that runs the accessibility checker on both builds, known-violations.json) so the flag-off baseline comparison stays green. The lead's notes win over this brief and the manifest where they differ (they say nothing on this slice beyond the standing rules and one note for step 32 on the baseline sampler, which this slice must not break: difference 8): <scratchpad>/ws01-lead-notes.md. The manifest entry (order 27) is in <scratchpad>/ws01-manifest.json. node_modules is installed; nothing ever runs against a remote database or the Cloudflare account; agents never commit, stash, reset or check out anything; the working tree is the only copy.

Environment facts for this container: the pinned Playwright expects a Chromium build the container does not have, so every npm run test:a11y here runs as PW_CHROMIUM_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium npm run test:a11y (the config reads that variable); never run playwright install; WRANGLER_SEND_METRICS=false on every wrangler command; localhost is exempt from the outbound proxy, so the a11y servers on 127.0.0.1 work. Dependencies are exact-pinned (no caret) at versions at least two weeks old, with package-lock.json updated by npm install; this slice needs no new package. The branch tip is a12c74e (slice 26), and the working tree is clean when the slice starts; origin/redesign/ws01-design-system carries a74f221 (slice 25) in this container until the lead pushes, and the local main ref is 4c1a466 and does not carry the checkpoint merges, so a diff against the local main shows far more than this slice: take this slice's own changes as the working tree against a12c74e.

Build exactly this. Make chess data read correctly: halves as ½, tabular mono figures, colour shown by shape and word, and real table headers.

src/components/ResultCell.tsx renders the result letter, a tint, a colour marker and the opponent number, for example "W ○ 17". The marker is an inline SVG circle, hollow for White and filled for Black, because the monospace face's latin subset has no ○ or ● glyphs. The cell's accessible name reads like "Won with White against 17".

src/components/ui/table.tsx:
- TableHead defaults to scope="col"
- a new TableRowHeader renders th scope="row"
- Table gains a stickyFirst prop that pins the first column with an opaque surface token in every scope
- Table gains an optional bounded scroll container with a sticky header, so long tables stay together on the page
The new props are opt-in; adding scope="col" changes no rendering.

Crosstable.tsx and StandingsTable.tsx (now in src/areas/live/components) change only with newLook on:
- scores and tiebreaks use formatScore
- figures use font-mono (the new look's monospace face, under data-look=new) with tabular-nums
- the player cell is a row header
- the first column is sticky on narrow screens
- Crosstable renders round cells through ResultCell, drops the separate w/b line, and adds a legend that names the markers in words
- the em dash placeholder for a missing tiebreak becomes a plain hyphen with an aria-label

With newLook off, both tables render exactly as today. Under the flag, check the other score renderers on the pairings and print pages (TournamentPairingsPage, TournamentPrintPage, ResultsEntry) and switch any half-point display to formatScore.

Only the new look changes what a visitor sees. With newLook off both tables render the markup they render today, with one allowed difference: scope="col" on their header cells, which changes nothing visible (the step 32 brief allows an ungated scope attribute if it is listed). The manifest says both that the two tables change only with newLook on and that with it off their markup is unchanged apart from the added scope attribute; read them together that way, and record the choice as a deviation. The manifest's risk stands: TableHead is a shared primitive, so every default it gains reaches every caller of src/components/ui/table.tsx, which today is the fixture page alone (difference 1); the new Table props are opt-in and change no class an existing caller gets. With newLook on the new look reaches three pages, through the components they already draw: /tournaments/:id/pairings, /tournaments/:id/print and the manage page (Crosstable, StandingsTable and ResultsEntry). git diff against a12c74e shows changes under src/pages only in TournamentPairingsPage.tsx, TournamentPrintPage.tsx and the fixture page.

Verify items from the manifest, each to be re-checked against the tree as it is now (the earlier finding follows): 3.5 today. (Crosstable.tsx:11 and StandingsTable.tsx:9 both define fmt = n % 1 === 0 ? String(n) : n.toFixed(1); Crosstable uses font-mono (OS default) and prints colour as a bare w/b letter under the cell. Re-checked: lines 11 and 9 are as the finding says, and they feed Crosstable's Total cell (89), StandingsTable's Pts cell (54) and its four tiebreak cells (58). font-mono is on the result code only (Crosstable 80, with text-xs), not on the Rating or Total cells, and StandingsTable has no font-mono at all; both tables carry tabular-nums on the table element (Crosstable 53, StandingsTable 31), so font-variant-numeric is already tabular-nums in every cell with newLook off, and the figures change face only where font-mono is added. Colour is the bare letter in a block span (Crosstable 85, text-[10px] in the muted ink at 70 per cent, below the 12px floor the boards use), the cell's title attribute White or Black (78) and the legend line under the table (95 to 97). Two things the finding leaves out: StandingsTable's placeholder for a missing tiebreak is an em dash at line 58 (the type says tiebreaks is always there; the code guards for it), and with newLook off both tables must keep it.) Marker glyph coverage. (The monospace face and the two heritage faces, latin subsets, contain U+00BD but not U+25CB or U+25CF, so markers must be SVG or CSS shapes. Re-checked: the unicode-range of each of the monospace face's six files in node_modules (latin, latin-ext, cyrillic, cyrillic-ext, vietnamese, symbols2) covers U+00BD in the latin file only and neither U+25CB nor U+25CF in any of them, so the finding holds for the face the site uses; a character no file covers falls back to the device's font, which is why the markers are drawn. The glyph test beside the format tests already finds the face whose range covers U+00BD and reads the latin file's character map (lines 96 to 123): it proves U+00BD present and U+25CB absent in that one file and says nothing of U+25CF or the other five files, so extend it to hold both markers outside every file's range. The two heritage faces are not on the tree: package.json lists the sans, the monospace face, the display accent and the two broadcast faces only, and step 30 adds them, so that part of the finding can be neither checked nor pinned here; say so in the record.)

Further differences between the manifest's assumptions and the tree, all measured at the working tree this slice starts from (slice 26 finished, HEAD a74f221 when measured). (1) The table primitives have one caller. src/components/ui/table.tsx (117 lines) is imported by src/pages/fixtures/ScopeFixturePage.tsx line 25 and by nothing else: one Table, three TableHead, no row header. Every real table is a plain table element: 13 of them in 9 files (Crosstable.tsx 53, StandingsTable.tsx 31, ResultsEntry.tsx 136, TournamentPrintPage.tsx 90 and 159, TournamentManagePage.tsx 1334, 1624 and 2281, TournamentDetailPage.tsx 634 and 660, ScannerPage.tsx 813, MembersTable.tsx 180, ChampionsPanel.tsx 129), with 68 plain th elements (69 with the primitive's own); scope appears on four of them, all in ScannerPage.tsx (816 to 818 and 824), and on no chess table. So TableHead's default scope and a new TableRowHeader change nothing a visitor reaches, and the manifest's sentences about Crosstable and StandingsTable (the player cell is a row header; the first column is sticky) cannot come from the primitives unless those tables are drawn through them. Decide and record: the flag-off branch of each table is the file's current markup, unchanged but for scope="col" on its th (the test holds today's markup as a literal copy), and the flag-on branch is drawn through the primitives or by hand. Drawing it through Table swaps the wrapper: today it is a div with overflow-x-auto, a 12px radius, a border and print:overflow-visible (Crosstable 52, StandingsTable 30) inside a break-inside-avoid block (50 and 28), while Table's is a relative w-full overflow-auto div (table.tsx 9) that takes no class of its own, so Table needs a way to carry those classes. The pairings page draws no table element at all (its rounds are lists).

(2) The first column is not the player. Crosstable's first cell is the pairing number (header at line 56, cell at 68) and the player is second (57 and 69 to 72); StandingsTable's first is the place (34 and 49 to 51) and the player second (35 and 52). The row header the manifest asks for is the second cell, and a pinned first column alone keeps the number or place on screen while the names scroll off, the opposite of the point: decide and record (pin both with the second offset by the first's width, pin the player and move the number inside it, or another way). A pinned cell needs an opaque ground in every look. A surface token is opaque everywhere (#fff on the plain :root, and #fff, #111a2c, #0e1526, #fff and #fffdf8 in base, dark, live, scholastic and heritage); --hairline is a translucent white in dark and live (index.css 465 and 510), so it is no ground. The headers' bg-muted/50 (Crosstable 55, StandingsTable 33), the first-place row's bg-lca-gold/5 (StandingsTable 48) and the row hover tint (table.tsx 61) are all translucent: a pinned cell in the tinted row must carry the tint over its opaque ground or the row shows a gap, and a pinned cell hides the hover tint unless it takes it too. Row borders of a collapsed table do not travel with a pinned cell, so check the row lines while scrolled at a narrow width (the tables hold a 480 and a 560 pixel minimum, Crosstable 53 and StandingsTable 31). Sticky positions against the nearest scrolling ancestor, which in the real tables is the overflow-x-auto div that never scrolls vertically, so a sticky header does nothing without Table's bounded container (a max height, an overscroll-contained, keyboard-focusable named region as ScrollPanel is, and a header on an opaque surface token), the area step 26 handed to this slice.

(3) Score sites, measured. formatScore has no caller under src (zero); it reaches src through src/lib/format.ts (one line, export * from the domain folder) and domain/format/index.ts line 5, and it is tested in test/unit/format.test.ts, format-edges.test.ts, test/integration/domain-format.test.ts and the seed test (seed-fixtures-edges.test.ts 344). Six places write a numeric score or tiebreak, in four files, with four separate formatters: Crosstable.tsx 89 (Total, through fmt at line 11), StandingsTable.tsx 54 (Pts) and 58 (the four tiebreak columns), both through fmt at line 9, TournamentPrintPage.tsx 104 and 109 (a player's score going into the round, through its own fmt at 33) and TournamentManagePage.tsx 2304 (the US Chess report's Total, an inline toFixed(1)). Four of the six draw a point today (2.5 as 2.5); the print page's two already draw ½ with newLook off, because its fmt turns .5 into ½ (line 106 does the same for a drawn game, 1/2-1/2 to ½-½). So switching the print page to formatScore gives the same text for every whole and half score chess produces and differs only for a value that is neither (2.25 stays 2.25 where its fmt rounds to 2.3); gate it on newLook like the rest, so nothing with the flag off needs arguing. The manage page's report table (2281 to 2318) is the director's report for US Chess, not a standings table, and is not in this slice's files: leave the page alone and record line 2304 as a follow-up for WS08 (the CSV the page exports, line 149, writes the raw number and must stay numeric). The manage page does change with newLook on through the components it draws (ResultsEntry 2154, StandingsTable 2228, Crosstable 2229).

(4) The other renderers' half points are already ½ and are results, not scores: ResultsEntry.tsx 15 (the quick button ½-½, which is also a result string) and 155 (½ point (requested)), TournamentPairingsPage.tsx 31 (a half-point bye) and 114 (½ pt), TournamentPrintPage.tsx 106. So ResultsEntry needs no half-point change (its manifest listing is for its four header cells, 139 to 142, at most). The one place a half shows as a fraction is the public pairings list: formatResult (Pairings 28 to 36) has no case for a draw, so a drawn game draws the stored text 1/2-1/2 at line 120, with newLook on or off; under newLook make it ½-½, as the print page and the results entry already write it. formatScore cannot do this (a string that is not a number comes back as given), so a small mapping in the page file does. Half symbols under src: 25 on 14 lines in 9 files; the scanner's decoder, types and normaliser and their two tests hold 13 on 6 lines in 5 files and are not display copy, the fixture page's two lines are 3½ and 2½, and the three chess files hold the other 10 on 6 lines.

(5) Colour today. Crosstable draws a bare w or b under each result (85) and the words White or Black only in the cell's title attribute (78); its legend (95 to 97) ends w / b color. The print page's pairing sheet and ResultsEntry head their columns White and Black (Print 94 and 96, ResultsEntry 140 and 141); the print page's alphabetical sheet has a Color column with the words White, Black and Bye (76, 77, 165, 175); the public pairings list puts white first with a vs between (Pairings 105 to 109) and says no colour word; the manage page's pairing editor labels its two fields (2088 and 2103). The result codes Crosstable draws are W, L, D, B (full-point bye), H (half-point bye), X and F (forfeit win and loss), U (not played, also a game with no opponent) and an empty code for a pending game that still shows the opponent's number and colour; cellFor (15 to 33) is the one reader of the pairings and stays so. The board draws a not-played cell as a dashed outline on the surface, not a tint.

(6) The record already promises the markers. Decisions line 922 (White and Black markers (step 27)) says they are small images because the monospace file has no ○ or ●. Keep that bullet under its heading, add Done in step 27, and say what was built: inline SVG circles, a ring for White and a filled disc for Black, in the words' colour, hidden from screen readers with the cell's name carrying the colour in words, so the cell never relies on colour or shape alone for a reader. Also keep the ScrollPanel bullet (line 921) word for word and add the table area after it (see the recorder paragraph).

(7) Where AC6 is proved. The standings and the crosstable are on /tournaments/fx-t-done/pairings (the standings view by default, the crosstable behind the tab buttons at Pairings 268 to 283, shown when a score is above zero, line 199), on /tournaments/fx-t-done/print?what=standings and ?what=crosstable, and on the manage page; /tournaments/fx-t-done itself, the page the manifest's wording points at and the one the baseline samples, draws neither (its two tables are the round schedule at 634 and the sections at 660, and its one monospace element, line 755, is a rating). The seed (scripts/seed/fixtures.sql 156 to 166) gives one section, Open, five players and three rounds with a draw in every round, a full-point bye and two half-point byes, and the totals 2.5, 2, 1.5, 1.5 and 0.5 (seeded-data.spec.ts 220 to 227), so the scores include halves. The spec checks ½ and the computed font-family and font-variant-numeric on those pages on a11y-on, and that a11y-off still shows 2.5 with the device's monospace stack and the same tabular numerals, so it asserts different things on the two builds. The live look is on a11y-on only: its rules sit under data-look new, so setting data-theme on a11y-off changes nothing.

(8) The baseline and the step 32 note. test/a11y/baseline.ts samples the first visible main th and the first main .font-mono on each of four routes, and finds either only on /tournaments/fx-t-done: the th reads Section (TournamentDetailPage.tsx 663, a plain th, navy, no background, the sans face) and the monospace element reads 1910 (line 755, muted ink, the device's monospace stack); on /, /tournaments and /membership neither is found, and baseline.ts counts was missing, now found as a difference. None of this slice's files is drawn on any of the four routes, so the table work cannot move the baseline provided that no stylesheet rule outside the new look touches th or .font-mono, no th or font-mono appears on those pages, and TournamentDetailPage.tsx is left alone. Any table header change belongs under newLook or keeps its computed colour and font. The lead's note for step 32 (the last section of the lead's notes) records that the accessibility job failed once on a74f221 and passed on a rerun: baseline.ts sampled /tournaments/fx-t-done after the local database answered "database is locked" to the page's data request, so the page drew its error text (the first Button a plain outline button, no table header, no monospace element) and the comparison read a colour change. Step 32 owns the fix (waiting for the page's content, one retried navigation); this slice must not take it on and must not break the sampler: leave baseline.ts and baseline.json alone, add no request to that page, and make the spec you write wait for the content it reads (a table row), not for network idle alone. If baseline.ts fails with that signature (the page drawing its error, a lock in a server's log) and no colour or font difference, rerun the whole run once, quote both runs, and never rewrite baseline.json; a failure with a real colour or font difference is a defect in the slice. Step 26's runs met the same lock twice (follow-up line 1354).

(9) Browser pins that this slice's own change breaks. (a) test/a11y/print-look.spec.ts line 131 reads the crosstable's player cell as table tbody tr td.font-medium; once that cell is a th with newLook on, the selector matches nothing and the test throws; change it to read either element, keeping the navy and 4.5:1 expectations (lines 118 to 140), and keep line 43 (the pairing sheet's td:nth-child(2) span) true by not restructuring that sheet. (b) test/a11y/seeded-data.spec.ts 209 to 228 reads the standings rows with tr.querySelectorAll('td') and takes the place, player and points from cells 0, 1 and 3; with the player a th on a11y-on the cells shift and the test fails there (the spec runs on both builds); read th and td together, in document order. (c) test/a11y/builds.spec.ts pins the fixture page: exactly 3 th (104), the td.font-mono texts 3½, 3 and 2½ (141 and 142), the page text free of a digit, a point and a 5 (143, on both builds), the monospace face (148) and the column headers Place, Player, Score (150). (d) test/a11y/tokens.spec.ts 137 reads the first main .font-mono on /tournaments/fx-t-done with newLook off (the detail page's rating, in the device's monospace stack) and 211 the first main td.font-mono on the fixture (the new look's monospace face on a11y-on); a new td.font-mono placed before the fixture's Standings table must still be in that face on a11y-on.

(10) The fixture page. The manifest's file list leaves it out, but Table's new props (the row header, the pinned column, the bounded container) have no other drawn consumer, and a browser test needs one in each look; the real tables cannot go on it, because the page's text is held free of a point and a 5 on both builds (builds.spec.ts 143) and the flag-off tables print 2.5. So draw the Table props and ResultCell cells there with whole numbers and no points, and test the real tables on the seeded pages. The gold guard pins the fixture's StatusBadge places by line (test/unit/goldText.test.ts 799 to 804: lines 114, 115, 116, 213, 217 and 218), so add the content after line 218, at the end of the fragment BaseComponents returns (the file ends at line 281) or in a component below it, or update those pins in the same change; step 26's pins on the fixture also hold the count of [data-status] elements (13), the five Buttons, the three th and the three td.font-mono texts, so a new section either keeps those counts or the specs that hold them (builds.spec.ts, scope-switch.spec.ts, scope-switch-edges.spec.ts, test/unit/redesign-status-step26.test.ts) move with it. The page is also scanned for an en or em dash character and for the old initials of US Chess (browser-test-wiring.test.ts 456 to 490): the hyphen that stands for a missing tiebreak is a hyphen.

(11) Unit pins the new code meets. test/unit/base-components-scope.test.ts pins the importers of ScrollPanel to the fixture page (line 52) and ADMIN_SCROLL to its value and its ten uses in nine admin files (80 to 98), so table.tsx imports neither: write the bounded container's classes in the file, or move the pins in the same change. test/unit/contrast.test.ts 698 to 728 holds every text-status class in a TSX file to sit beside its own tint and lists them by line; a ResultCell that uses one joins that list, and in the live look --status-full is gold (index.css 530) and --status-soon is near white (528) while --ok and --bad stay green and red (512 and 513), so tint a win, a loss and a draw from ok, bad and the closed pair (or let the letter and the marker carry it) and have the contrast test hold each pair in every look. test/unit/raw-colours.test.ts, semantic-map.test.ts and goldText.test.ts read the whole tree: no palette colour, hex, bg-white or gold text on a light ground in the new classes, and the print page's two border-gray-300 rules (allowlist line 36) and its text-quiet-600 words (read by print-look.spec.ts) stay as they are. A new form of an already mapped class moves their pinned counts, so run them. There is no snapshot anywhere in test (no toMatchSnapshot, no __snapshots__ folder) and no unit test draws Crosstable, StandingsTable, ResultsEntry, the two pages or ui/table.tsx: the flag-off test holds today's markup as a string copied from the file as it stands before you edit it, and the flag is flipped inside one test file with the hoisted getter of test/unit/news-pinned-flag.test.tsx (lines 15 to 29), which also draws both ways and compares. The component test opts into the DOM environment the way status-dot-newlook.test.tsx does.

(12) The accessibility checker has not run on these pages. No spec runs it on /tournaments/:id/pairings or the print page (seeded-data.spec.ts only reads rows; the checker runs on the fixture page in components.spec.ts and on /, /tournaments and /membership elsewhere), so the first run is this slice's: a finding outside the tables (for instance in the tab buttons or the navy hero) is recorded, and fixed if it is token-level or under newLook; nothing goes in known-violations.json. Base is the page as it is; live is a data-theme of live set on the page's main through the page (a11y-on only). Not measured here, since the checker never ran on these pages: Crosstable's and StandingsTable's scroll wrappers are overflow-x-auto with a minimum width above a phone's and hold nothing a keyboard reaches, which is what the checker's scrollable-region-focusable rule looks for, so run it at a phone width (390 pixels) and make the flag-on scroll region focusable and named (tabIndex 0, role region, an aria-label naming the section's table) as ScrollPanel does; that changes markup, so it is flag-on only. An aria-label on a span with no role is a prohibited attribute in ARIA 1.2: give ResultCell's name through hidden text or a role the checker accepts, and let the checker decide. The word the manifest gives (Won with White against 17) needs a form for each code: the byes, a forfeit, not played and a pending game.

(13) Printing. src/index.css has no print rule; print fit rests on utilities (print:overflow-visible on both wrappers, break-inside-avoid, and print:text-black on the print page, line 120), and step 24's dark and live looks sit inside screen-only rules, so a printed page takes the light look (follow-up line 1366). The monospace face is wider than the proportional one, and print:overflow-visible lets a table that is too wide run off the paper instead of scrolling. Measure the printed crosstable (emulated print media at a US Letter portrait width) on the seed's three rounds and say at how many rounds it stops fitting, then keep a wider one on the page (smaller figures or a wrap under print) rather than clipped; add no rule outside data-look new.

(14) The date line of REDESIGN_STATUS.md.
